questions.prompt: The philosopher lived many years at Athens, teaching eager young men.
questions.answer: Philosophus multōs annōs Athēnīs habitāvit, iuvenēs studiōsōs docēns.

questions.prompt: The exile, having set out from Italy, sought safety at Athens.
questions.answer: Exsul, ex Italiā profectus, salūtem Athēnīs petīvit.

questions.prompt: At Delphi the priestess used to answer those who questioned her.
questions.answer: Delphīs sacerdōs eōs quī interrogābant respondēbat.

questions.prompt: In the whole camp a terrible plague was raging that night.
questions.answer: Tōtīs castrīs illā nocte dīra pestilentia saeviēbat.

questions.prompt: At this place the ancient queen hid the ivory statue.
questions.answer: Hōc locō rēgīna antīqua eburneum signum occultāvit.

questions.prompt: In one part of the city the people, terrified, pitied the dying.
questions.answer: Ūnā parte urbis populus territus morientēs miserābātur.

questions.prompt: In these places the ancient walls, overthrown by age, still stand.
questions.answer: Hīs locīs mūrī antīquī, vetustāte ēversī, adhūc stant.

questions.prompt: The sterns of the ships rest on the shore, bound by their anchors.
questions.answer: Stant lītore puppēs, ancorīs religātae.

questions.prompt: In the shady woods the mouse lay hidden, fearing the fierce owl.
questions.answer: Silvīs opācīs mūs latēbat, ferum būbōnem timēns.

questions.prompt: On the high mountains the snow gleams white throughout the long winter.
questions.answer: Montibus altīs nix candet alba per longam hiemem.

questions.prompt: The messenger returned from the city, worn out by the long journey.
questions.answer: Nūntius ex urbe rediit, longō itinere fessus.

questions.prompt: The stoic departed from Rome, despising the riches of the wealthy.
questions.answer: Stōicus Rōmā discessit, dīvitiās dīvitum contemnēns.

questions.prompt: Having been driven from his fatherland, he wandered from city to city.
questions.answer: Ex patriā pulsus, ab urbe ad urbem errāvit.

questions.prompt: The sailors, having weighed anchor, set out from Carthage.
questions.answer: Nautae, sublātā ancorā, Carthāgine profectī sunt.

questions.prompt: Throughout the whole city the kindness of the generous man was praised.
questions.answer: Tōtā urbe virī līberālis līberālitās laudābātur.

questions.prompt: In the whole house the poison had been hidden by the cruel stepmother.
questions.answer: Tōtā domō venēnum ā crūdēlī novercā occultātum erat.

questions.prompt: At Carthage the great queen, mourning, consoled the wretched.
questions.answer: Carthāgine rēgīna magna maerēns miserōs cōnsōlābātur.

questions.prompt: In that place, over a long age, the sick slowly recovered.
questions.answer: Illō locō longō aevō aegrī lentē convalēscēbant.

questions.prompt: At Carthage the merchants amassed great riches through cunning.
questions.answer: Carthāginī mercātōrēs magnās dīvitiās calliditāte comparāvērunt.

questions.prompt: In this place, fortified by a thick wall, the citizens felt safe.
questions.answer: Hōc locō, dēnsō mūrō mūnītī, cīvēs tūtī sē sentiēbant.

questions.prompt: The weary king set out from Italy, his kingdom having been abandoned.
questions.answer: Rēx dēfessus ex Italiā profectus est, rēgnō relictō.

questions.prompt: On the shore stand the pine ships, dear to the weary rowers.
questions.answer: Lītore stant pīneae nāvēs, fessīs remigibus cārae.
